items.title: Give (or refuse) consent to the rent increase
items.quote: Wir bitten Sie um Ihre Zustimmung, das Nutzungsentgelt ab dem 01.02.2027 um 10 % auf 434,50 € zu erhöhen. Ihre Antwort benötigen wir bis Ende Januar 2027.
items.computation: This is a rent-increase request (Mieterhöhungsverlangen) under § 558 BGB, delivered by hand to the letterbox on Wed 18.11.2026, 8:50 Uhr (stated receipt date; no authority deemed-delivery rule applies since it was handed over directly). Under § 558b Abs. 1, 2 BGB the tenant may consent until the end of the second calendar month after receipt. Receipt falls in November 2026; the first calendar month after is December, the second is January 2027, so the period ends 31.01.2027. 31.01.2027 is a Sunday, so under § 193 BGB the deadline shifts to the next business day, Monday 01.02.2027. (The landlord's own wording 'bis Ende Januar 2027' is one day earlier than the statutory deadline but does not disadvantage the tenant.)

items.title: New rent (434,50 €) takes effect, if consent is given
items.quote: das Nutzungsentgelt ab dem 01.02.2027 um 10 % auf 434,50 € zu erhöhen
items.computation: The letter states the increased rent is to apply from 01.02.2027, the calendar date printed in the letter, conditional on the tenant's consent.

warnings: The landlord's stated reply deadline ('bis Ende Januar 2027') falls on a Sunday; the statutory deadline under § 558b BGB and § 193 BGB is actually Monday 01.02.2027 — one day later, so this does not disadvantage the tenant, but the written wording should not be relied on as the exact legal cut-off.
No formal signed consent form (Zustimmungserklärung) is included in the text provided; the letter asks for it to be returned, but its content could not be checked here.

This is a civil-law request between the cooperative and its member, not an administrative decision, so there is no Rechtsbehelfsbelehrung and no appeal deadline — if the tenant does not consent, the cooperative would have to sue for consent within a further three months (§ 558b Abs. 2 BGB), which is the landlord's own deadline, not the tenant's.
